svg.title: Schematic tuning and qualitative perturbation effects
svg.desc: Three-panel schematic. A: six synthetic single-cell tuning examples: a place field (one localized firing region), a grid cell (fields on a triangular lattice with sixfold symmetry), a head-direction polar curve peaking near northeast, a border response along the east wall, a boundary-vector band set 0.30 of the arena width inside the east wall with two oppositely facing animal markers that share equal eastward vectors to the wall, and a firing curve that rises with running speed. B: two joint-tuning heatmaps, each one schematic neuron: position by head direction, and head direction by running speed. C: two separate perturbation studies: medial entorhinal lesions (Hales et al., 2014) leave hippocampal place fields but reduce their precision and long-term stability; temporary hippocampal inactivation (Bonnevie et al., 2013) disrupts grid periodicity in entorhinal grid cells. Arrows show perturbation effects, not anatomical pathways.

g.text: Schematic examples: each plot shows one illustrative cell; map colors are normalized within each cell.
One example: firing rises with speed
B: One cell can combine variables
Example cell I: position × head direction
One neuron: fires at one place, mainly when facing east
Example cell II: head direction × speed
One neuron: fires when facing east, more at higher speed
A neuron’s firing can depend on more than one variable.
C: Perturbations reveal influence in both directions
Arrows show perturbation effects, not individual anatomical pathways.
Schematic tuning and qualitative perturbation effects
